column3: 숙제를 자꾸 미루다 보니 일이 많아졌어요.
column4: I kept putting off my homework, and now I have a lot to do.
column5:
Conj: 미뤄요 · 미뤘어요 · 미룰 거예요 · 미루는 N · 미뤄서
Use: N을/를 미루다 · 약속을 미루다, 내일로 미루다
cf) 연기하다 = more formal (postpone an event)

column2: make plans, set up a meeting
column4: I made plans with a friend this weekend.
column5:
Conj: 잡아요 · 잡았어요 · 잡을 거예요 · 잡는 N · 잡아서
Use: N이랑/하고 약속을 잡다 · 날짜를 잡다, 일정을 잡다
cf) 약속이 있다 = already have plans

column3: 바쁘실 텐데 시간 내 주셔서 감사해요.
column4: You must be busy, so thank you for making time.
column5:
Conj: 내요 · 냈어요 · 낼 거예요 · 내는 N · 내서
Use: 시간을 내다 · 시간 내 주셔서 감사해요 (very common thank-you)

column3: 회의랑 수업 시간이 겹쳐서 하나는 못 가요.
column4: My meeting and class overlap, so I can't go to one of them.
column5:
Conj: 겹쳐요 · 겹쳤어요 · 겹칠 거예요 · 겹치는 N · 겹쳐서
Use: N이/가 겹치다 · 일정이 겹치다, 약속이 겹치다

column4: It's not easy to match schedules with my friend.
column5:
Conj: 맞춰요 · 맞췄어요 · 맞출 거예요 · 맞추는 N · 맞춰서
Use: 일정을 맞추다 · 시간 맞춰서 가다 (arrive on time) · 알람을 맞추다
cf) 맞다 = to be correct/fit (no object)

column4: What's your schedule like next week?
column5:
Use: 일정을 잡다/짜다 · 일정이 바쁘다 · 여행 일정
cf) 스케줄 = same, casual loanword

column4: I've had a bit more free time lately.
column5:
Use: 여유가 있다/없다/생기다 · 시간 여유, 마음의 여유
여유롭다 = relaxed, leisurely (ㅂ irregular: 여유로워요)

column3: 비가 오는 걸 핑계로 하루 종일 집에 있었어요.
column4: I used the rain as an excuse to stay home all day.
column5: Use: 핑계를 대다 = make an excuse · N을/를 핑계로 · 핑계 대지 마세요

column2: when it actually comes to it
column4: When I actually went, it was more fun than I expected.
column5:
Adverb. Contrast between what you expected and what happened.
Use: 막상 V-(으)니까 / 막상 V-(으)려고 하니까

column2: if possible, unless there's a good reason
column3: 웬만하면 주말에는 일 안 하려고 해요.
column4: If I can help it, I try not to work on weekends.
column5:
Adverb. Softens a plan or request.
Use: 웬만하면 V-(으)려고 해요 · 웬만하면 V-(으)세요

column2: be a hassle, can't be bothered
column4: Maybe because I'm tired, I can't be bothered to cook.
column5:
Conj: 귀찮아요 · 귀찮았어요 · 귀찮을 거예요 · 귀찮은 N · 귀찮아서
Use: V-기 귀찮다 · N이/가 귀찮다 · 귀찮게 하다 = bother someone

column3: 친구가 제 생일을 잊어버려서 좀 서운했어요.
column4: My friend forgot my birthday, so I felt a little hurt.
column5:
Conj: 서운해요 · 서운했어요 · 서운할 거예요 · 서운한 N · 서운해서
Use: N한테 서운하다
cf) 섭섭하다 = almost the same · 실망하다 = disappointed (more general)

column4: We couldn't understand each other, so it was really frustrating.
column5:
Conj: 답답해요 · 답답했어요 · 답답할 거예요 · 답답한 N · 답답해서
Use: 마음이 답답하다 (frustrated) · 방이 답답하다 (stuffy room)

column4: I'm going on a trip tomorrow and I'm already excited.
column5:
Conj: 설레요 · 설렜어요 · 설렐 거예요 · 설레는 N · 설레서
Use: 마음이 설레다 · 설레는 마음
cf) The dictionary form is 설레다, not 설레이다

column4: I got scolded for something I didn't do, so it felt unfair.
column5:
Conj: 억울해요 · 억울했어요 · 억울할 거예요 · 억울한 N · 억울해서
Use: Said when you're blamed or treated unfairly · 억울한 일을 당하다

column4: Shall we go for a walk to clear our heads?
column5: Use: 기분 전환하다 · 기분 전환 겸 N/V = partly to refresh yourself · 기분 전환이 되다

column4: That friend is really quick to read the room.
column5: Use: 눈치가 빠르다/없다 · 눈치를 보다 = watch others' reactions · 눈치 채다 = notice

column4: The traffic was so bad that I got annoyed.
column5: Use: 짜증(이) 나다 = get annoyed · 짜증을 내다 = take it out on someone · 짜증나다 is often written as one word

column2: I know, right / tell me about it
column4: I know, it's really hot today.
column5:
Expression. Agrees with what someone just said. Very common reply.
Casual: 그러게 · Also 그러게 말이에요

column4: There's a sale today? No wonder there were so many people.
column5:
Adverb. Said when you learn the reason for something you noticed.
Often with -더라고요 (#35) or -더라

column3: 손님이 오기 전에 방을 치워야 해요.
column4: I have to clean up my room before the guests come.
column5:
Conj: 치워요 · 치웠어요 · 치울 거예요 · 치우는 N · 치워서
Use: 방을 치우다 · 상을 치우다 = clear the table
cf) 정리하다 = organize · 청소하다 = clean (dust, wipe)

column4: I've been busy, so the dishes have piled up.
column5:
Conj: 쌓여요 · 쌓였어요 · 쌓일 거예요 · 쌓이는 N · 쌓여서
Use: N이/가 쌓이다 · 스트레스가 쌓이다, 일이 쌓이다
cf) 쌓다 = to stack (takes an object)

column3: 세탁기가 고장 나서 빨래를 못 했어요.
column4: The washing machine broke, so I couldn't do laundry.
column5:
Conj: 고장 나요 · 고장 났어요 · 고장 날 거예요 · 고장 난 N · 고장 나서
Use: N이/가 고장 나다 (machines) · 고치다 = fix
cf) 깨지다 = break (glass, plates)

column3: 화장실 전구가 나가서 새 걸로 갈았어요.
column4: The bathroom bulb went out, so I replaced it with a new one.
column5:
Conj: 갈아요 · 갈았어요 · 갈 거예요 · 가는 N · 갈아서 (ㄹ irregular)
Use: 전구를 갈다, 물을 갈다 · 갈아타다 = transfer (subway)
cf) 바꾸다 = change (general)

column4: Folding laundry is the most annoying chore.
column5:
Conj: 개요 · 갰어요 · 갤 거예요 · 개는 N · 개서
Use: 빨래를 개다, 이불을 개다
cf) 접다 = fold (paper)

column4: Water leaked, so mold grew on the wall.
column5: Use: 곰팡이가 생기다/피다 · 곰팡이 냄새

column4: We split the housework half and half.
column5:
Use: 집안일을 하다/돕다/나누다
cf) 가사 = formal word for housework

column3: 이번 달 관리비가 생각보다 많이 나왔어요.
column4: This month's maintenance fee came out higher than I expected.
column5: Use: 관리비가 나오다 = the bill comes · 관리비를 내다 · 월세 + 관리비

column4: I didn't have time, so I just ate something quick for breakfast.
column5: Adverb. Use: 대충 하다/먹다/알다 · 대충 몇 시? = roughly what time?

column4: After moving, my place is a complete mess.
column5: Use: 엉망이다 · 엉망이 되다 · 엉망진창 = total chaos (casual)

column2: take on, be in charge of
column4: I ended up being in charge of this project.
column5:
Conj: 맡아요 · 맡았어요 · 맡을 거예요 · 맡는 N · 맡아서
Use: 일을 맡다, 역할을 맡다 · also 냄새를 맡다 = smell

column4: I worked late all week, so I'm completely worn out.
column5:
Conj: 지쳐요 · 지쳤어요 · 지칠 거예요 · 지친 N · 지쳐서
Use: N에 지치다 · 일에 지치다
cf) 피곤하다 = tired · 지치다 = drained

column4: I did all my backed-up homework over the weekend.
column5:
Conj: 밀려요 · 밀렸어요 · 밀릴 거예요 · 밀린 N · 밀려서
Use: 일이 밀리다 · 밀린 N = overdue N · 차가 밀리다 = traffic is backed up

column4: The café is noisy, so I can't concentrate.
column5:
Conj: 집중해요 · 집중했어요 · 집중할 거예요 · 집중하는 N · 집중해서
Use: N에 집중하다 · 집중이 안 되다 = can't focus

column4: These days I'm getting by on coffee.
column5:
Conj: 버텨요 · 버텼어요 · 버틸 거예요 · 버티는 N · 버텨서
Use: N(으)로 버티다 · 끝까지 버티다
cf) 참다 = hold back, endure (feelings, pain)

column3: 내일이 마감이라서 오늘 늦게까지 일해야 해요.
column4: Tomorrow is the deadline, so I have to work late today.
column5:
Use: 마감일 · 마감이 다가오다 · 마감하다 = close (shop), end
cf) 기한 = time limit (more formal)

column3: 이번 주에는 야근을 세 번이나 했어요.
column4: I worked late three times this week.
column5:
Use: 야근하다 · 야근이 많다
cf) 칼퇴근 = leaving right on time (slang)

column4: I eat lunch with my coworkers.
column5:
Use: 직장 동료, 회사 동료
cf) 동기 = someone who started at the same time

column4: I woke up late and barely caught the bus.
column5: Adverb. Use: 겨우 V-았/었어요 = barely managed · 겨우 N = only N (겨우 만 원)

column2: kind of, more than you'd think
column4: This job is surprisingly tough.
column5:
Adverb. Something is quietly or unexpectedly so. Very common in speech.
Often with -더라고요 (#35)

column4: Maybe because it was the weekend, the restaurant was really crowded.
column5:
Conj: 붐벼요 · 붐볐어요 · 붐빌 거예요 · 붐비는 N · 붐벼서
Use: N이/가 붐비다 · 사람들로 붐비다
cf) 사람이 많다 = more casual way to say it

column4: It's a popular place, so we waited in line for a whole hour.
column5:
Conj: 서요 · 섰어요 · 설 거예요 · 서는 N · 서서
Use: 줄을 서다 · 줄이 길다 · 줄 서서 기다리다

column4: I can't be bothered today, shall we order chicken?
column5:
Conj: 시켜요 · 시켰어요 · 시킬 거예요 · 시키는 N · 시켜서
Use: 음식을 시키다 · 배달을 시키다 · N한테 일을 시키다
cf) 주문하다 = order (more formal)

column4: I ate so much I'm stuffed.
column5:
Conj: 배불러요 · 배불렀어요 · 배부를 거예요 · 배부른 N · 배불러서 (르 irregular)
Use: 배불러 죽겠어요 = I'm stuffed · 배가 부르다 also common

column4: The pizza was a bit greasy, so I had a coke.
column5:
Conj: 느끼해요 · 느끼했어요 · 느끼할 거예요 · 느끼한 N · 느끼해서
Use: 음식이 느끼하다 · also 말이 느끼하다 = cheesy, slimy (person)

column4: Does Korean food suit your taste?
column5:
Use: 입맛이 없다 = no appetite · 입맛에 맞다 = suits your taste
cf) 취향 = taste in general (style, hobbies)

column4: This is my regular café.
column5: Use: 단골 가게, 단골손님 · 단골이 되다

column3: 이 동네에 맛집 아는 데 있어요?
column4: Do you know any good restaurants in this neighborhood?
column5: Use: 맛집을 찾다 · 유명한 맛집 · 맛집 투어

column4: I got promoted, so today's on me.
column5:
Conj: 한턱내요 · 한턱냈어요 · 한턱낼게요 · 한턱내는 N · 한턱내서
Use: Said when celebrating something · cf) 쏘다 = treat (slang: 제가 쏠게요)

column4: I want to sleep as much as I want this weekend.
column5: Adverb. Use: 실컷 자다/먹다/놀다/울다

column3: 어제 라면 먹고 자서 얼굴이 많이 부었어요.
column4: I ate ramen before bed last night, so my face is really puffy.
column5:
Conj: 부어요 · 부었어요 · 부을 거예요 · 부은 N · 부어서 (ㅅ irregular)
Use: 얼굴이 붓다, 다리가 붓다 · also 붓다 = pour (물을 붓다)

column3: 하루 종일 앉아 있어서 어깨가 뻐근해요.
column4: I sat all day, so my shoulders are stiff.
column5:
Conj: 뻐근해요 · 뻐근했어요 · 뻐근할 거예요 · 뻐근한 N · 뻐근해서
Use: 어깨가/목이/허리가 뻐근하다
cf) 아프다 = hurts (stronger)

column3: 너무 빨리 먹어서 체한 것 같아요.
column4: I ate too fast, so I think I have indigestion.
column5:
Conj: 체해요 · 체했어요 · 체할 거예요 · 체한 N · 체해서
Use: 급하게 먹다가 체하다 · Common complaint in Korea, often treated with 소화제

column4: If you have a cold, don't push yourself.
column5:
Conj: 무리해요 · 무리했어요 · 무리할 거예요 · 무리하는 N · 무리해서
Use: 무리하지 마세요 = take it easy · 무리예요 = that's too much, impossible

column3: 약을 먹고 푹 자서 많이 나았어요.
column4: I took medicine and slept well, so I got a lot better.
column5:
Conj: 나아요 · 나았어요 · 나을 거예요 · 낫는 N · 나아서 (ㅅ irregular)
Use: 감기가 낫다 · 빨리 나으세요 = get well soon · also A: 이게 더 나아요 = this is better

column4: I've felt achy and run down since yesterday.
column5: Use: 몸살이 나다 · 몸살 기운이 있다 = feel like you're coming down with something

column3: 저녁을 늦게 먹어서 소화가 안 돼요.
column4: I ate dinner late, so I can't digest it.
column5: Use: 소화가 잘 되다/안 되다 · 소화제 = digestive medicine · 소화하다

column4: I'm not feeling great today.
column5: Use: 컨디션이 좋다/안 좋다 · 컨디션 관리 = taking care of yourself

column4: I rested well at home over the weekend.
column5: Adverb. Use: 푹 쉬다, 푹 자다 · 푹 쉬세요 = get some good rest

column4: Thanks to your concern, I'm all better.
column5:
Use: N 덕분에 · V-(으)ㄴ 덕분에 · 덕분에요 = thanks to you (reply)
cf) -(으)ㄴ 탓에 (#7) = because of (bad result)

column3: 요즘 돈을 아끼려고 도시락을 싸 와요.
column4: These days I bring a packed lunch to save money.
column5:
Conj: 아껴요 · 아꼈어요 · 아낄 거예요 · 아끼는 N · 아껴서
Use: 돈을/시간을 아끼다 · 아끼는 물건 = treasured item

column4: Don't waste money on useless things.
column5:
Conj: 낭비해요 · 낭비했어요 · 낭비할 거예요 · 낭비하는 N · 낭비해서
Use: N을/를 낭비하다 · 시간 낭비 = waste of time

column4: I'm saving up money to go on a trip.
column5:
Conj: 모아요 · 모았어요 · 모을 거예요 · 모으는 N · 모아서 (ㅡ drops)
Use: 돈을 모으다 · 사람들을 모으다
cf) 모이다 = gather (no object)

column4: Moving cost a lot of money.
column5:
Conj: 들어요 · 들었어요 · 들 거예요 · 드는 N · 들어서 (ㄹ irregular)
Use: V-는 데 돈이/시간이 들다 · 힘이 들다 = be hard

column3: 여기는 다른 데보다 가격이 저렴한 편이에요.
column4: Prices here are on the cheaper side compared to other places.
column5:
Conj: 저렴해요 · 저렴했어요 · 저렴할 거예요 · 저렴한 N · 저렴해서
cf) 싸다 = cheap (more casual) · 저렴하다 sounds more polite

column4: The movie was so boring that it felt like a waste of money.
column5:
Conj: 아까워요 · 아까웠어요 · 아까울 거예요 · 아까운 N · 아까워서 (ㅂ irregular)
Use: 돈이/시간이 아깝다 · 버리기 아깝다 = too good to throw away

column4: Students can get a 20% discount.
column5:
Use: 할인을 받다 · 할인하다 · 할인 쿠폰
cf) 세일 = sale (event)

column4: You need a receipt to get a refund.
column5: Use: 영수증을 받다/챙기다 · 영수증 드릴까요? = do you want the receipt?

column4: The size didn't fit, so I got a refund.
column5:
Use: 환불하다 · 환불받다 · 환불이 안 되다
cf) 교환 = exchange

column3: 괜히 샀어요. 그냥 싼 걸 살걸 그랬어요.
column4: I shouldn't have bought it. I should have just bought the cheap one.
column5:
Adverb. Use: 괜히 V-았/었어요 = regret doing something pointless
Pairs well with -(으)ㄹ걸 그랬다 (#40)
